paper.abstract_en: In this proceeding, I review recent theoretical developments in small-$x$ spin physics and discuss prospects for measurements at the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). Topics covered include: (1) helicity evolution at small $x$ through double-logarithmic resummation and phenomenological implementations in JAMsmallx global analyses; (2) orbital angular momentum and its extraction through Generalized Parton Distributions and Wigner distributions; (3) single transverse spin asymmetries in the small-$x$ regime, including the interplay between the Sivers effect, gluon saturation, and the lensing mechanism; and (4) quantum entanglement and Bell nonlocality in deep inelastic scattering processes at the EIC. These studies demonstrate how the EIC will provide unique opportunities to probe the three-dimensional structure of nucleons, test fundamental aspects of QCD dynamics in the nonperturbative regime, and explore the quantum nature of parton interactions through entanglement measurements. Building upon the tremendous successes of the LHC and RHIC programs in unveiling the quantum nature of matter at the most fundamental level, the advent of the EIC on the horizon can unravel even more profound puzzles involving the internal structure of protons and hadrons, ushering in a precision era for nuclear and particle physics.
